title: Editorial guidance says nothing about what a headline, deck and blurb are for
description: Writing a Machines on Machines article on 2026-11-04, the live editorial context and editorial pack contained no guidance on headlines, decks or blurbs, and the copywriting skill does not mention them. story_writing.py says only that the blurb is two or three lines for listings. The result was a question headline on an article that makes a claim, and the editor corrected it. Ryan's rule from that correction: an article that has a point says it in the headline, the subtitle explains it in more detail, and the blurb is a different text that appears in listings. Add this to publication policy and the copywriting skill, decide whether it is per publication or standard, and add a check.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Done for Machines on Machines on 2026-11-04: Ryan's rules are now in that publication's policy data through sections doctrine set: educated lay reader in the style of Scientific American, inverted pyramid, pointed questions, skimmability, pull quotes, figure placeholders, and what a headline, subtitle and blurb are for. Other publications are untouched. Still open: the copywriting skill and DRAFT_INSTRUCTIONS should tell writers to read these from policy, and whether any of it becomes a standard default.
